basis: Nematode infection; skin, ocular and visceral involvement varies across subtypes, with no single organ consistently affected across the umbrella.
Intellectual disability and developmental delay define the disorder; myopia affects 6/9 patients. Hypotonia does not establish primary muscle damage.
Adipocytic soft-tissue sarcoma, usually arising in deep soft tissue; a palpable subcutaneous nodule does not establish skin involvement. Visceral effects are occasional.
Carcinoma confined to endometrium, a reproductive organ outside the axes.
Immune-mediated infantile ulcerative colitis; anemia and motor delay reported in one patient do not establish direct extraintestinal organ damage.
Excess precursor load overwhelms trimethylamine metabolism; the definition does not establish liver injury.
Acute ketoacidosis is an acid-base metabolic disorder; vomiting and abdominal pain do not establish gastrointestinal damage.
Defective airway clearance causes bronchiectasis in 4/4; recurrent otitis media affects 3/3. Secondary infections do not make this an immune disorder.
Typically occupies abdominal peritoneum and omentum; hepatic dissemination with hepatomegaly is common (30-79%). Nodal spread does not establish blood or marrow disease.
Nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing impairment affects 8/8 patients.
Fungal infection umbrella; anatomical sites vary across subtypes, without a consistently affected additional organ.
Lymphoid-cell malignancy arising in the small intestine; lymphoma also requires the infectious_immune mechanism axis.
Severe ID and joint/skeletal defects define syndrome; urethral hypospadias 80-99%; oral clefts/intestinal defects 30-79%. Strabismus 30-79% omitted at cap.
Carcinoma arises in tonsillar oropharyngeal mucosa; the pharynx belongs to the pulmonary axis. Referred ear pain does not establish ear damage.
Persistent skin pigmentation abnormalities define Legius syndrome; specific learning disability is frequent (30-79%). Other organ abnormalities are uncommon.
Glomus tumor arising in the skin; local vascular differentiation does not establish systemic cardiovascular disease.
Complex I metabolic defect with lactic acidosis; neurologic developmental impairment 3/6 and cardiomyopathy 2/6. Optic atrophy 1/6; nystagmus alone does not prove eye damage.
Cavernous vascular lesion arising in brain or meninges; abnormal blood vessels and CNS location define it. It is not a blood-cell neoplasm.
Neurologic, hepatic and hearing dysfunction each commonly exceed 30% across Zellweger spectrum; retinal, enamel and nail abnormalities omitted at cap.
Craniosynostosis and radial-ray defects define syndrome; malabsorption 30-79%; poikiloderma 2/6. Proptosis alone does not establish ocular functional damage.
Hair loss and nail dystrophy define the ectodermal dysplasia. Inguinal hernia is a separately diagnosed associated anomaly.
Excessive erythrocytosis and chronic hypoxemia define the syndrome; pulmonary hypertension occurs in some cases, and thrombotic risk alone does not establish vascular damage.
Progressive epilepsy/neurodegeneration with ceroid-storage classification; visual loss is usually 5-29%. Optic atrophy in 1/2 is insufficient to generalize across the disorder.
Bone marrow hypoplasia and congenital neurologic abnormalities, including callosal agenesis and hydrocephalus, define the syndrome.
Recessive intellectual disability with motor delay and spasticity; no evidence of a separate directly affected organ.
